title: What Is a Facility Hygiene Audit?
excerpt: A facility hygiene audit is a structured evaluation of hygiene controls, records and actual practice against defined requirements to identify conformity, gaps and improvement needs.
seo_title: What Is a Facility Hygiene Audit? | Alle's ClinX
meta_description: Learn what a facility hygiene audit reviews, how evidence is gathered and how findings support corrective action and improvement.
content_html:
A facility hygiene audit is a planned, documented evaluation of whether hygiene-management requirements are being implemented and maintained. It reviews both the management system and evidence from actual operations.

Define the audit scope and criteria

The audit should state which areas, processes, records and requirements are included and what standards will be used for evaluation.

Gather objective evidence

Evidence can include observations, interviews, schedules, training records, inspection data, chemical controls, equipment records and corrective-action documents.

Audits often use sampling

An audit may not review every record or task. Sampling should be appropriate to risk and large enough to support reasonable conclusions.

Document conformity and non-conformity

Findings should be linked to evidence and the applicable requirement so the facility can understand exactly what is working and what needs correction.

Follow-up is part of the audit cycle

Significant findings should lead to corrective action, ownership, due dates and verification that actions were completed and effective.

Practical takeaway

A hygiene audit is not just an inspection of visible cleanliness. It evaluates whether the system, records and real-world practice collectively meet defined requirements.
